notes: One entry per README claim. claim is the sentence the README states, word for word; check is how the judge proves it; params may read deployments/testnet.json through ${path} templates, and a claim whose template is still null prints SKIP (pending), never PASS.
mode full marks a build or test step: it runs with --full or --step <id>, not in the default two-minute pass.
evidence is the file node judge/capture.mjs writes and node judge/judge.mjs --offline replays.

Reads that must give the same answer whenever a judge runs (a verdict with a TTL, counters a later run could move) are pinned to a block recorded in deployments/testnet.json and go to archival RPC. Current-state claims (keys, config, oracles) are read at finality final and assume the owners do not re-key, freeze or re-policy after capture; see judge/README.md.

claims.claim: Circle's USDC on NEAR testnet (3e2210e1...cb8af) reports NEP-141 metadata: spec ft-1.0.0, symbol USDC, 6 decimals.
Circle's testnet USDC answers is_blocklisted, one of the signals the verdict engine reads (aid-demo-merchant.testnet: false).
Circle's USDC on NEAR mainnet (17208628...36133a1) answers is_blocklisted, so the same signal works on real mainnet accounts (read-only).
Arras's ERC-8004 identity registry, identity-registry.erc-8004.near, is a deployed contract on NEAR mainnet (read-only signal source).
Arras's ERC-8004 reputation registry, reputation-registry.erc-8004.near, is a deployed contract on NEAR mainnet (read-only signal source).
a-identity.testnet, the registry owner, exists on NEAR testnet.
oracle.a-identity.testnet, the oracle that writes verdicts, exists on NEAR testnet.
aid-demo-owner.testnet, the vault owner, exists on NEAR testnet.
aid-demo-merchant.testnet, the legitimate demo payee, exists on NEAR testnet.
aid-demo-attacker.testnet exists on NEAR testnet; it was created during setup and is not a demo payee (a payee named attacker proves nothing about a classifier).

aid-demo-agent.testnet is not the agent: it predates the keyless vault and holds one full-access key and no function-call key; every agent transaction in this table is signed by the vault account with its function-call key instead.
registry.a-identity.testnet runs the committed build: its on-chain code_hash is base58(sha256) of deployments/wasm/a_identity_registry.wasm.
vault.aid-demo-owner.testnet runs the committed build: its on-chain code_hash is base58(sha256) of deployments/wasm/agent_spend_policy.wasm.
The vault account holds no full-access key: every key on it is a function-call key for exactly pay, request_payment and record_refusal on the vault, with a finite NEAR allowance.
The oracle account holds no full-access key: it writes verdicts only with a function-call key on the registry limited to set_verdict, set_verdicts, clear_verdict and clear_reports.
The registry account holds no full-access key, so nobody can redeploy or delete the registry.
The registry owner's key list is public and small: a-identity.testnet holds exactly one full-access key and no function-call key.

The vault's on-chain policy is the one stated: owner aid-demo-owner.testnet, Circle testnet USDC, registry registry.a-identity.testnet, not frozen, unknown payees held, and the daily cap and per-payment ceiling recorded in deployments/testnet.json.
Only oracle.a-identity.testnet may write verdicts: the registry's oracles() is exactly [oracle.a-identity.testnet].
The registry's owner is a-identity.testnet, whose key stays offline.
registry.a-identity.near on NEAR mainnet runs the CI reproducible build: its code_hash is base58(sha256) of deployments/wasm-mainnet/a_identity_registry.wasm.
vault.a-identity.near on NEAR mainnet runs the CI reproducible build: its code_hash is base58(sha256) of deployments/wasm-mainnet/agent_spend_policy.wasm.
registry.a-identity.near holds no access key at all, so nobody can redeploy or delete it.
vault.a-identity.near holds no full-access key: its only key is the agent's function-call key for exactly pay, request_payment and record_refusal on the vault, with a finite NEAR allowance.
The mainnet vault's policy is owner a-identity.near, Circle's mainnet USDC, registry registry.a-identity.near, not frozen, unknown payees held, a 5 USDC daily cap and a 2 USDC per-payment ceiling.
oracle.a-identity.near holds no full-access key: it writes verdicts only with a function-call key on registry.a-identity.near limited to set_verdict, set_verdicts, clear_verdict and clear_reports.
Only oracle.a-identity.near may write verdicts on mainnet: the registry's oracles() is exactly [oracle.a-identity.near].

On mainnet the oracle judged linear-protoco1.near, a name one character off LiNEAR's token that does not exist, DENY from public chain data and wrote it with its function-call key: verdict_set with verdict DENY.

On mainnet the agent's payment to linear-protoco1.near after the oracle's DENY was refused by the vault contract: payment_refused with reason RegistryDeny and source registry, and no receipt reached the USDC contract.
On mainnet the oracle judged linear_protocol.near, a cited fake-airdrop account that another team's public registry flags, WARN and wrote it: verdict_set with verdict WARN.
On mainnet the agent's payment to linear_protocol.near after the oracle's WARN was held by the vault for its owner: payment_held with kind registry_warn, and no receipt reached the USDC contract.

The registry's verdict for the lookalike aid-demo-merchamt.testnet, read at the block recorded in deployments/testnet.json, is DENY with reason codes, written by the oracle, and its evidence names the snapshot, block and engine it was computed from.
The merchant's first payment waited for the owner: the agent's request_payment to aid-demo-merchant.testnet emitted payment_held, and no receipt reached the USDC contract.
The owner approved that first payment once, with one owner_pay (1 yoctoNEAR): payment_sent with by_owner true, and a nep141 ft_transfer moved the USDC from the vault to aid-demo-merchant.testnet.

The agent paid aid-demo-merchant.testnet with its function-call key and USDC moved: payment_sent, and the USDC contract executed a nep141 ft_transfer from the vault to the merchant for the exact amount.
The agent's guard refused the lookalike aid-demo-merchamt.testnet and recorded it on chain: record_refusal emitted payment_refused with source agent_guard, and nothing moved.

A compromised agent that skipped the guard and paid the lookalike, which nobody had judged yet, was held by the vault contract for the owner: payment_held with reason UnknownPayee, and no receipt reached the USDC contract.
The oracle judged the lookalike DENY from public chain data and wrote it with its function-call key: set_verdict signed by oracle.a-identity.testnet with that key, verdict_set with verdict DENY.
Paying the lookalike again was refused by the vault contract on chain: payment_refused with reason RegistryDeny and source registry, and no receipt reached the USDC contract.
The owner's approval does not override a later DENY: owner_pay of the held lookalike payment was refused on chain with RegistryDeny (held_settle_failed), and nothing moved.
For aid-demo-printshop.testnet, a vendor nobody has history with, the agent asked the owner instead of paying: request_payment emitted payment_held, and nothing moved.
The owner approved the vendor's held payment with one owner_pay (1 yoctoNEAR): payment_sent with by_owner true, and a nep141 ft_transfer moved the USDC from the vault to the vendor.
A payment above the per-payment ceiling was refused by the vault contract on chain: payment_refused with reason AboveAutoApprove and source policy, and nothing moved.

aid-demo-merchant.testnet is a payee the vault knows from its own payments: at the block recorded after the demo, paid_count equals the payment_sent events to it in the demo's transactions, one of them the owner's approval (by_owner true).

The vault counts registry refusals only: at the block recorded after the demo, refusal_count(aid-demo-merchamt.testnet) equals the payment_refused events with reason RegistryDeny and source registry in the demo's transactions (at least the agent's pay and the owner's owner_pay).

Refusals an agent records are counted apart from registry refusals: at the same block, guard_refusal_count(aid-demo-merchamt.testnet) equals the payment_refused events with source agent_guard in the demo's transactions, and none of the registry's refusals.
The agent key cannot call the USDC contract: the protocol rejected its ft_transfer on USDC with ReceiverMismatch, before execution.
The agent key cannot attach a deposit, so no 1-yoctoNEAR method is reachable: the protocol rejected pay with 1 yoctoNEAR attached (DepositWithFunctionCall), before execution.
The agent key cannot call an owner method: the protocol rejected set_registry on the vault with MethodNameMismatch, before execution.
The agent key cannot give itself more power: the protocol rejected adding a full-access key to the vault account (RequiresFullAccess), before execution.
The agent key cannot move the vault's NEAR: the protocol rejected a 1 yoctoNEAR transfer out of the vault (RequiresFullAccess), before execution.

Anyone can recompute the lookalike's verdict: the SDK's offline verdict on the snapshot the oracle saved gives the registry's DENY at the recorded block, with the same reasons and evidence string, and every block-pinned chain read in that snapshot is what archival RPC returns.

An x402 payment settled on NEAR testnet through A-Identity's own relayer: x402-relayer.a-identity.testnet signed one Delegate action from aid-demo-agent.testnet holding exactly one ft_transfer with 1 yoctoNEAR, and the USDC contract executed a nep141 ft_transfer of exactly 10000 (0.01 USDC) from aid-demo-agent.testnet to a-identity.testnet, with no failed receipt.
No NEAR secret key, private_key field or PEM private key is committed under near/.
Everything under near/ was committed inside the hackathon window (2026-10-19 to 2026-11-14 UTC), and nothing under near/ exists at the pre-hackathon tag.
The registry and vault unit tests pass: cargo test -p a-identity-registry -p agent-spend-policy --locked.
